title: A Promise for the Summer
premise: Wendell Dravenmoor, a pastry chef drowning in debt, agrees to pose as the girlfriend of Elias Thorne—a wealthy stranger she meets by accident—to survive his family's brutal summer reunion at Coldwater House. What begins as a transactional lie deepens as Wendell discovers Elias is being pressured to sign away his late mother's estate, and that his family's kindness comes with invoices. When her café faces final foreclosure and Elias's deception is exposed mid-reunion, both must choose between the safe lies that kept them invisible and a costly truth. In the end, Wendell loses the café but wins back her voice, Elias forfeits his inheritance to keep his integrity, and they meet again—on time this time—at her small new bakery, where staying past the last train finally feels like a promise kept.
about_author: Theo Coldharbour is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing in the margins of order tickets before turning to fiction full-time. Known for romances set in kitchens and coastal towns, Coldharbour writes about people who mistake survival for living.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A foreclosure notice arrives at Dravenmoor's Café on the morning of its best sales day, and Wendell pastes on a smile for customers while calculating how many weeks she has left. The beat is quiet desperation masked as competence—establishing her pride, her debt, and her habit of shrinking to survive.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Ordered Twice
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Elias Thorne returns three times in one day, ordering things he clearly doesn't want, and finally admits he's hiding from a phone call about his mother's estate. Their banter sparks something unguarded in Wendell. The beat is reluctant connection between two people fluent in avoidance.

chapters.title: An Offer With Fine Print
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias proposes the fake relationship: accompany him to the month-long Thorne family reunion at Coldwater House, room and board included, plus a payment that would clear her debt. He tells himself it's practical. The beat is self-deception—he notices her laugh and files it under 'logistics.'

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell negotiates hard—half up front, no kissing clause, an exit anytime—and signs despite every instinct screaming that rich families eat people like her. The beat is wary hope; she lets herself imagine the café saved, which makes the risk feel worth it.

chapters.title: Coldwater House
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Arrival at the reunion: marble halls, subtle cruelty, and Vivienne Thorne, the matriarch, whose welcome is a velvet appraisal. Wendell performs 'girlfriend' badly until Elias takes her hand and something in the performance turns real for half a second. The beat is impostor terror laced with first thrill.

chapters.title: The Family Recipe
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At dinner, the family pressures Elias to sign papers transferring Coldwater House to his uncle Marcus's development company—'for everyone's good.' Elias deflects, watching Wendell charm the kitchen staff with pastry talk. The beat is the theme of inheritance made explicit: love in this family is conditional on signatures.

chapters.title: Lessons in Belonging
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Rehearsing their history together on the boathouse dock, invented memories start feeling load-bearing. Elias mentions his mother taught him to bake; Wendell teaches him properly, flour on both their hands. The beat is intimacy through shared craft—the fake story becoming a true one.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Invitation
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The matriarch privately offers Wendell money to leave before the reunion ends, revealing she knows the relationship is staged—and hinting she knows about Wendell's debts. Wendell refuses, stunned by her own defiance. The beat is the first time Wendell chooses visibility over safety.

chapters.title: What Marcus Wants
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Uncle Marcus corners Elias with a threat: sign, or he'll dig into Wendell's finances and expose the arrangement publicly, humiliating them both. Elias realizes his family has been investigating her all along. The beat is protective fury—and the dawning knowledge that he's in too deep to call this fake.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. After a near-kiss interrupted by family, Wendell almost flees on the evening train, ticket in hand. She watches it leave without her and walks back to Coldwater House in the dark. The beat is the blurb's central image realized: choosing to stay when leaving was easy.

chapters.title: Midsummer Gala
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The reunion's centerpiece gala: Wendell bakes a dessert course that steals the evening, earning genuine respect from guests and quiet pride from Elias. But Marcus uses the crowd to announce the estate sale vote. The beat is triumph shadowed by encroaching threat—her best night inside a tightening trap.

chapters.title: Kitchens at Midnight
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Unable to sleep, Elias finds Wendell stress-baking at midnight. They trade truths: her father's failure and shame around money, his mother's death and the guilt of inheriting instead of grieving. The kiss happens here, unhurried and chosen. The beat is vulnerability rewarded.

chapters.title: Paper Trails
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell discovers documents in Elias's study showing Marcus forged their mother's signature years ago—the inheritance itself is built on fraud. She must decide whether to tell Elias, knowing it will detonate his family. The beat is moral weight: truth as a weapon with collateral damage.

chapters.title: The Foreclosure Call
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Her bank calls: final notice, seven days. Elias offers to pay it outright; Wendell refuses, hearing her father's shame in her own ears. They fight about pride versus partnership. The beat is the romance's central conflict crystallized—she can accept help surviving, but not rescue.

chapters.title: Vivienne's War
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Vivienne reveals she hired investigators on Wendell not out of cruelty but to test whether Elias would fight for someone—something he never did for himself. She warns him Marcus won't stop at exposure. The beat is the antagonist-matriarch complicated: power wielded as twisted pedagogy.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the family assembly, Marcus detonates everything: the contract, the payments, Wendell's debts, read aloud before forty relatives. Wendell stands alone as the room turns. Elias hesitates one beat too long before speaking. The beat is public humiliation—the price of survival exacted in front of witnesses.

chapters.title: The Longest Silence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Elias defends her fiercely but too late; Wendell, humiliated that he needed prompting, packs to leave. He asks her to stay; she says staying for someone isn't the same as staying for yourself. The beat is heartbreak with dignity—love present but insufficient.

chapters.title: Signing Away
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone, Elias confronts Marcus with the forged signature evidence Wendell left behind, then refuses to sign the transfer, forfeiting his inheritance and his place in the family. Vivienne, watching, finally smiles. The beat is climax of the power theme: he chooses integrity over legacy.

chapters.title: Empty Ovens
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Back home, Wendell closes the café for good, boxing up her mother's mixing bowls. Grief, but also clarity: the café was her father's dream, not hers. The beat is loss transmuted into identity—she stops surviving someone else's life.

chapters.title: What She Bakes For Herself
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Weeks later, Wendell signs a lease on a tiny bakery of her own design, funded partly by the money she earned and refused to return. First batch sold out by noon. The beat is rebuilding on her own terms—inheritance redefined as what you make, not what you're given.

chapters.title: The Man at the Counter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Elias appears at her new bakery, having taken a job as a teacher, owning nothing but his choices. He doesn't ask for a second chance; he orders twice, like the first day, and waits. The beat is courtship renewed as equals—no contracts, no fine print.

chapters.title: A Promise for the Summer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Late summer, closing time: Wendell flips the sign, and Elias stays past the last train without either of them checking the schedule. She offers him a key—not to her home, but to the bakery, a share in something built honestly. The beat is resolution: two people who learned that staying visible, and staying put, are the same brave act.
